soundness_flags.label: Gaussian experimental model / all frontier statements
soundness_flags.one_line: P_{\mu,\sigma} is used as a uniquely indexed law although the assumptions give only Gaussian marginals, not a joint law for (Y(0),Y(1)); define the observed-data law explicitly or include the within-unit coupling in the model and establish copula invariance of the risk.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper establishes an average-propensity efficiency benchmark and logarithmic-batch linear-functional second-order upper and matching lower rates under nuisance-rate assumptions.
The paper gives a two-stage competitive-ratio result and an unrestricted adaptive lower ratio 1+(1/480)T^{-1}.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Theorem 4.3 and Theorem E.1 (HTML lines 392--403 and 1239--1247)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Uniform regret is inverse-square-root over the bounded class, improves to inverse-pilot on standard deviations bounded away from zero, and the broad-class pooled pilot plan has n^(2/3) pilot scale.
BOLS asymptotic normality is stated under their conditions, with the extension to unequal batches requiring the smallest batch size to diverge and batch size independent of history.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Make P_{\mu,\sigma} an explicit observed-data law (or add a bivariate Gaussian/copula parameter and prove its irrelevance) before attempting any risk or minimax proof.
State a focused non-Gaussian or bounded-outcome extension criterion showing which part of the every-B frontier depends only on variance learning rather than Gaussian exactness.
Add a small worked exact-count instance that computes the allocation lattice penalty and the deterministic-prefix rule, making the operational overscheduling mechanism immediately auditable.

recommended_next_step: Revise the model specification to make the risk functional unambiguous, then advance the exact-B frontier and growing-B inference targets to Stage 0.
